title: Transport of free profinite internal-function resolutions to section modules
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small skeleton of profinite sets with the topology generated by finite jointly surjective continuous families [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring object of $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, with sheafified objectwise tensor [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], and write $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for its section-ring sheaf. Let $E:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\mathrm{sec}})$ be the section-action equivalence [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Use relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For profinite $P$, let $R[P]$ be the free internal module on $h_P(V)=C(V,P)$ and let $L_P$ be the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{h_P(V)}R_{\mathrm{sec}}(V)$. Put $H_P=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_R(R[P],-)$ and $G_P=\mathcal Hom_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}(L_P,-)$ [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom, def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then $\mathcal C$ is subcanonical and has finite products. There are canonical isomorphisms $E(R[P])\cong L_P$, natural covariantly in $P$ and equal to the identity on free generators, and $E H_P\cong G_P E$, natural covariantly in modules and contravariantly in $P$, characterized by the corresponding evaluation pairings. In the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] they induce
$$D(E)RH_P(M[0])\cong RG_P(E(M)[0]),$$
computed on every nonnegative injective resolution of $M$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The equivalence preserves injective resolutions and colimits and carries every augmentation-preserving lift of a module map to its section-action lift. Consequently it identifies the localized termwise-colimit comparison for any compatible diagram of such resolutions with the corresponding comparison for $G_P$, including all coprojection maps. The functor $U:\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\mathrm{sec}})\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ is exact and faithful, preserves colimits and detects quasi-isomorphisms; filtered colimits in both module categories are exact.

proof.text: The terminal one-point space and binary topological products are profinite: compactness of a product follows from [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact]; distinct pairs are separated in one Hausdorff factor, and products of clopen basis sets form a clopen basis. The usual product maps have the continuous-map universal property, also after passing to a skeleton. For a finite covering family $S_i\to S$, the continuous surjection $q:\coprod_i S_i\to S$ has compact domain (take a finite subcover separately on each of the finitely many summands) and Hausdorff target. By [lem-sfb-compact-hausdorff-surjection-quotient] it is a quotient map. A matching family of continuous maps $S_i\to P$ is constant on each fibre of $q$: two points over the same point give maps from the one-point profinite space into $S_i,S_j$ with equal composites into $S$, so the matching condition on the generated sieve gives equality. Thus it defines a unique map $f:S\to P$. For every open $O\subseteq P$, $q^{-1}f^{-1}(O)$ is open, so the quotient criterion makes $f^{-1}(O)$ open. This proves the representable sheaf condition for the generating coverings and hence for their topology. The empty covering of the empty object gives its unique map to $P$.

The small-site hypothesis permits [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with coefficients $\operatorname{Ab}$: abelian sheaves form a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category, and the sheafification localization is monoidal. The hypotheses on tensor and size in [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] and [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] therefore hold. They give the section-action equivalence $E$, identity on underlying abelian sheaves and maps, additive and exact, with tensor comparison sending $m\otimes n$ to $m\otimes n$. By [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] the internal module category is Grothendieck abelian; by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] to $E$: it preserves injective objects, all small colimits, exact augmented resolutions, their augmentation-preserving lifts and homotopies. In particular the section-module category has enough injectives as well, by transporting an injective embedding along a quasi-inverse. The target is Grothendieck as well: $E$ carries a generator to a generator by full faithfulness, all colimits exist by equivalence, and a filtered colimit of short exact sequences is exact after applying the exact quasi-inverse, which preserves colimits.

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03EK (section-tensor-product); section-action tensor comparison; Homology Tag 015Z and injective equivalence transport

proof.text: By [def-sfb-condensed-free-module-adjunction], maps $R[P]\to N$ correspond to maps $h_P\to U_RN$ of condensed sets, with the correspondence given by the free-generator unit. For $F_P(V)=\bigoplus_{h_P(V)}R_{\mathrm{sec}}(V)$, a module-presheaf map $F_P\to E(N)$ is likewise exactly a natural assignment $b\mapsto s_b$: its value on $\sum_b r_b e_b$ must be $\sum_b r_b s_b$, and this formula gives the inverse. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] it factors uniquely through $L_P$. Since [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies the underlying sheaf of $N$ and $E(N)$, apply these correspondences to the universal generators to obtain inverse module maps $E(R[P])\rightleftarrows L_P$. Their composites fix the generators, so the same correspondences make them identities. Denote this isomorphism by $j_P$. For $u:P'\to P$ both $j_P E(R[u])$ and $L[u]j_{P'}$ send $e_b$ to $e_{u\circ b}$; hence they agree. This is covariance of the free-object comparison in $P$.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), the free-presheaf universal property and free internal-module adjunction

proof.text:
For an internal module $X$ and section module $A$, full faithfulness of $E$, [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom], the tensor comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], and $j_P$ give, naturally in $X,A$, the bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A,E H_PX)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E^{-1}A,H_PX)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R[P]\otimes_R E^{-1}A,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_P\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}A,EX).$$
By [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] the last set is $\operatorname{Hom}(A,G_PEX)$. Thus $EH_PE^{-1}$ and $G_P$ are right adjoints to the same functor $L_P\otimes-$. The uniqueness in [lem-weil-common-left-adjunctions-iso] yields $\beta_{P,X}:EH_PX\cong G_PEX$. Choose the unique isomorphism respecting the displayed adjunction bijections: its evaluation is the transported evaluation with $j_P$. Naturality in $X$ is part of the bijections. For $u:P'\to P$, precomposition with $R[u]$, respectively $L[u]$, has the same transpose because $j_P E(R[u])=L[u]j_{P'}$; injectivity of the adjunction bijections proves the required contravariant naturality. All local generator pairings are preserved since $j_P$ fixes generators and the tensor comparison fixes pure tensors. These additive functors preserve kernels directly: for any $d:X\to Y$ and test object $T$, adjunction identifies maps $T\to H_P(\ker d)$ with maps $R[P]\otimes_R T\to X$ killed by $d$, hence with maps $T\to H_PX$ killed by $H_Pd$. The same argument with $L_P$ proves this for $G_P$; zero objects and addition are preserved by their linear definitions. Thus both are left exact.

source.place: Tag 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), together with section-action tensor comparison and uniqueness of right adjoints

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] to the small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R_{\mathrm{sec}})$. It gives faithfulness and exactness of $U$ and preservation of all small colimits. Exactness gives $U\mathcal H^n(K)=\mathcal H^n(UK)$ via the preserved kernels and cokernels. If $Uf$ is a quasi-isomorphism, the kernel and cokernel of $\mathcal H^n(f)$ have zero underlying sheaf, hence are zero (faithfulness reflects zero objects: their identity maps are zero). Thus $f$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For a small filtered diagram of short exact module sequences, its underlying colimit sequence is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. Since $U$ preserves those colimits and reflects exactness by the same kernel/cokernel test, the module colimit sequence is exact. Exactness of filtered colimits in the internal category follows by $E$ and its inverse, which preserve colimits and exactness by step 2.

For any nonnegative injective resolution $a:M[0]\to I$, step 2 makes $E(a):E(M)[0]\to E(I)$ an injective resolution. The Hom functors are additive and left exact by the kernel calculation in step 4. By [lem-sp-kinjective-computes], a bounded-below injective complex is K-injective and computes the right derived functor. Applying $\beta$ degreewise gives a chain isomorphism $E H_P(I)\cong G_P(EI)$: compatibility with the differential is $\beta_{P,I^{n+1}} E(H_P(d^n))=G_P(E(d^n))\beta_{P,I^n}$. Exactness of $E$ supplies its derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Localizing this chain isomorphism therefore yields $D(E)RH_P(M[0])\cong RG_P(E(M)[0])$ in the ordinary derived category. For an augmentation-preserving lift $v:I\to J$ of $f:M\to N$, [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] identifies its image under each Hom functor with the derived arrow of $f$; degreewise naturality of $\beta$ makes the comparison square commute. It holds for every lift and every such resolution. Homotopies are preserved by the additive functors, so changes of lift do not change the localized arrow. Contravariant naturality in $P$ follows degreewise from step 4.

proof.text:
Let a small diagram of specified resolutions $I_i$ have a specified target resolution $I_\infty$ and compatible augmentation-preserving cocone lifts $v_i:I_i\to I_\infty$. Write $c_H:\operatorname{colim}_i H_P(I_i)\to H_P(I_\infty)$ for the induced termwise comparison. Step 2 identifies $E(\operatorname{colim}_i H_P(I_i))$ with $\operatorname{colim}_i E H_P(I_i)$ by the colimit isomorphism $\kappa$ characterized by the original coprojections. Let $B=(\operatorname{colim}_i\beta_{P,I_i})\kappa$. For each termwise coprojection $\iota_i$, naturality from step 4 says exactly
$$\beta_{P,I_\infty}E(c_H)E(\iota_i)=\beta_{P,I_\infty}E(H_P(v_i))=G_P(Ev_i)\beta_{P,I_i}=c_G B E(\iota_i).$$
Here $c_G$ is the comparison induced by the transported cocone $Ev_i$. The colimit universal property gives $\beta_{P,I_\infty}E(c_H)=c_G B$ as an equality of chain maps. This proves compatibility with every coprojection before localization, and functorial localization preserves that equality. Step 6 identifies the individual resolution terms with their derived images. In the filtered case step 5 additionally shows that termwise colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms, by commuting filtered colimits with the kernel/cokernel description of cohomology. No claim that an arbitrary unfiltered termwise colimit computes a derived colimit is used. For a compatible map of resolution diagrams $w_i:I_i\to J_i$ and target map $w_\infty$, one has $w_\infty v_i=v_i^Jw_i$. After $H_P$ or $G_P$ this gives $H_P(w_\infty)c_H=c_H^J\operatorname{colim}_iH_P(w_i)$ by testing coprojections. Naturality of $\beta$ identifies these squares under $E$. Parameter maps commute with the comparison by step 4, giving both asserted naturalities after localization.
